Read HDX-MS data from HDXExaminer or DynamX

Source: R/read_hdx.R
read_hdx.Rd

Reads an HDX-MS export into the table every HDXBoxeR function works on. The result can be passed wherever a function asks for filepath, e.g. output_tp(read_hdx("cluster.csv", fd = "Full Deuteration control")). Passing a file path directly also works; reading once is faster when several functions use the same data, and is needed for DynamX options such as fd.

Usage

read_hdx(
  path,
  format = c("auto", "hdxexaminer", "dynamx_cluster", "dynamx_state"),
  ...
)

Arguments

path

path to the csv file.

format

"auto" (default) detects the format from the header; or one of "hdxexaminer", "dynamx_cluster", "dynamx_state".

...

passed to read_dynamx() (e.g. fd, protein, combine_charges).

Value

data frame of class hdx_data in HDXExaminer's column layout.

Details

Supported formats (detected from the header line):

HDXExaminer

"All results" table export (read_hdxexaminer()).

DynamX cluster data

one row per peptide, state, exposure, raw file and charge (read_dynamx()); DynamX 2.x and 3.x. Raw files are the replicates.

DynamX state data

one averaged row per peptide, state and exposure. It holds no replicates, so it can be plotted but the replicate-based significance tests need cluster data.

Any other software: build the table from a long data frame with as_hdx_long().

See also

read_dynamx(), as_hdx_long()

Examples

file_nm <- system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
d <- read_hdx(file_nm)
a <- output_tp(d)
#> Protein.States used: Unbound bound
#> Deut.times used: 3.00s 60.00s 1800.00s 72000.00s
#> 29 peptide row(s) dropped: 29 not measured in every state, 0 with fewer than 2 replicate value(s)
#> Number of replicates used: Unbound=3 bound=3
#> no csv file written
